claim: Leptospirosis is the leading zoonotic disease in terms of morbidity and mortality worldwide.
source: Leptospirosis is the leading zoonotic disease in terms of morbidity and mortality worldwide.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract without supporting data or citations in this specific sentence.

claim: There are more than 300 serovars that can cause leptospirosis.
source: The key challenge has been developing a widely applicable vaccine that protects against the >300 serovars that can cause leptospirosis.
evidence: Statement about the number of serovars is presented as established knowledge.

claim: The fcpA- mutant has lost its ability to cause disease.
source: Although the fcpA- mutant has lost its ability to cause disease, transient bacteremia was observed.
evidence: References prior characterization study (Wunder et al., 2016a) and presents observational data.

claim: Transient bacteremia was observed after inoculation with the fcpA- mutant.
source: Although the fcpA- mutant has lost its ability to cause disease, transient bacteremia was observed.
evidence: Direct observation reported in the study.

claim: A single dose of the fcpA- mutant was sufficient to induce a robust anti-protein antibodies response in two animal models.
source: In two animal models, immunization with a single dose of the fcpA- mutant was sufficient to induce a robust anti-protein antibodies response that promoted protection against infection with different pathogenic Leptospira species.
evidence: Experimental results from the study's animal models.

claim: The fcpA- mutant promoted protection against infection with different pathogenic Leptospira species.
source: In two animal models, immunization with a single dose of the fcpA- mutant was sufficient to induce a robust anti-protein antibodies response that promoted protection against infection with different pathogenic Leptospira species.

claim: A small repertoire of biologically relevant proteins are highly conserved among pathogenic Leptospira species.
source: Furthermore, characterization of the immune response identified a small repertoire of biologically relevant proteins that are highly conserved among pathogenic Leptospira species and potential correlates of cross-protective immunity.
evidence: Results from proteome array analysis and sequence comparison.

claim: The Leptospira genus currently comprises 64 species.
source: Currently the Leptospira genus comprises 64 species with more than 300 serovars, with 17 of those species containing strains that can potentially cause severe disease in humans and animals (Casanovas-Massana et al., 2020; Vincent et al., 2019).

claim: 17 Leptospira species contain strains that can potentially cause severe disease in humans and animals.
source: Currently the Leptospira genus comprises 64 species with more than 300 serovars, with 17 of those species containing strains that can potentially cause severe disease in humans and animals (Casanovas-Massana et al., 2020; Vincent et al., 2019).

claim: A broad range of mammalian reservoirs harbor the spirochete in their renal tubules.
source: A broad range of mammalian reservoirs harbor the spirochete in their renal tubules shedding the bacteria in their urine for long periods of time (Thibeaux et al., 2017; Xu et al., 2016).

claim: Mammalian reservoirs shed Leptospira bacteria in their urine for long periods of time.
source: A broad range of mammalian reservoirs harbor the spirochete in their renal tubules shedding the bacteria in their urine for long periods of time (Thibeaux et al., 2017; Xu et al., 2016).

claim: The primary mode of transmission to humans is through contact with contaminated water or soil.
source: Leptospirosis is an environmentally transmitted disease with great health and economic impact in both humans and animals, for which the primary mode of transmission to humans is through contact with contaminated water or soil (Casanovas-Massana et al., 2018a).

claim: The large majority of the leptospirosis burden occurs in the world's most impoverished populations.
source: Although Leptospira has a worldwide distribution, the large majority of the burden occurs in the world's most impoverished populations (Costa et al., 2015), where the rapid growth of urban slums worldwide has created conditions for rat-borne transmission.

claim: The rapid growth of urban slums worldwide has created conditions for rat-borne transmission.
source: Although Leptospira has a worldwide distribution, the large majority of the burden occurs in the world's most impoverished populations (Costa et al., 2015), where the rapid growth of urban slums worldwide has created conditions for rat-borne transmission.
evidence: Inference based on cited literature and epidemiological understanding.

claim: Leptospirosis causes 1.03 million cases each year.
source: A recent study estimated that leptospirosis causes 1.03 million cases and 58,900 deaths each year (Costa et al., 2015).

claim: Leptospirosis causes 58,900 deaths each year.
source: A recent study estimated that leptospirosis causes 1.03 million cases and 58,900 deaths each year (Costa et al., 2015).

claim: Case fatality for Weil's disease is greater than 10%.
source: Case fatality for Weil's disease and LPHS is >10 and >50%, respectively, despite aggressive supportive care (Gouveia et al., 2008).

claim: Case fatality for LPHS is greater than 50%.
source: Case fatality for Weil's disease and LPHS is >10 and >50%, respectively, despite aggressive supportive care (Gouveia et al., 2008).

claim: The world's slum population will double to 2 billion by 2025.
source: The burden of leptospirosis will increase as climate and land use change continues to evolve and the world's slum population doubles to 2 billion by 2025 (UN-HABITAT, 2003).

claim: There is no effective control for leptospirosis.
source: However, there is no effective control for leptospirosis and safe and efficacious vaccines are not available for human use (Ko et al., 2009; Picardeau, 2017).

claim: Safe and efficacious vaccines are not available for human use.
source: However, there is no effective control for leptospirosis and safe and efficacious vaccines are not available for human use (Ko et al., 2009; Picardeau, 2017).

claim: China and Cuba use whole-cell vaccines in humans.
source: China and Cuba use whole-cell vaccines in humans (Yan et al., 2003; Martínez et al., 2004), but they are not licensed to be used elsewhere.

claim: Whole-cell vaccines used in China and Cuba are not licensed to be used elsewhere.
source: China and Cuba use whole-cell vaccines in humans (Yan et al., 2003; Martínez et al., 2004), but they are not licensed to be used elsewhere.

claim: Whole-cell vaccines are widely used for veterinary purposes.
source: Whole-cell vaccines are widely used for veterinary purposes but have significant limitations, since immunity is of short duration and predominantly humoral against LPS, which are serovar-specific moieties.

claim: Immunity from whole-cell vaccines is of short duration.
source: Whole-cell vaccines are widely used for veterinary purposes but have significant limitations, since immunity is of short duration and predominantly humoral against LPS, which are serovar-specific moieties.

claim: Immunity from whole-cell vaccines is predominantly humoral against LPS.
source: Whole-cell vaccines are widely used for veterinary purposes but have significant limitations, since immunity is of short duration and predominantly humoral against LPS, which are serovar-specific moieties.

claim: LPS are serovar-specific moieties.
source: Whole-cell vaccines are widely used for veterinary purposes but have significant limitations, since immunity is of short duration and predominantly humoral against LPS, which are serovar-specific moieties.

claim: Multivalent vaccines are unable to achieve sufficient coverage against the spectrum of serovars important for animal and human health.
source: Multivalent vaccines are unable to achieve sufficient coverage against the spectrum of serovars that are important for animal and human health (Adler, 2015).

claim: Conventional approaches have not yielded vaccine candidates.
source: To date, these conventional approaches have not yielded candidates and attempts have failed to identify a universal, widely applicable vaccine.
evidence: Summary of the state of the field based on established knowledge.

claim: Current control measures have been uniformly ineffective in addressing the large human and animal global health burden due to leptospirosis.
source: Current control measures have been uniformly ineffective in addressing the large human and animal global health burden due to leptospirosis, especially in developing countries.
evidence: Assessment based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Attenuation of Leptospira virulence has been long-recognized yet poorly understood.
source: Attenuation of Leptospira virulence has been long-recognized yet poorly understood phenomenon (Adler, 2015; Srikram et al., 2011).

claim: The inability to produce well-defined mutants has preempted efforts to identify a safe and efficacious attenuated-vaccine.
source: Until recently, the inability to produce well-defined mutants has preempted efforts to identify a safe and efficacious attenuated-vaccine.

claim: Current advances in genomic tools and whole-genome sequencing data for Leptospira have circumvented the limitation of producing well-defined mutants.
source: However, current advances in genomic tools and whole-genome sequencing data for Leptospira (Thibeaux et al., 2017; Picardeau, 2017) have circumvented this limitation and some promising results have been shown (Srikram et al., 2011; Murray et al., 2018).

claim: FcpA is a novel flagellar protein in the Leptospira genus involved in the composition of the sheath of the leptospiral flagella.
source: Recently, our group identified and characterized a novel flagellar protein in the Leptospira genus involved in the composition of the sheath of the leptospiral flagella, Flagella-coil protein A (FcpA).
evidence: References prior work by the authors.

claim: A mutant deficient in the fcpA gene lost its ability to produce translational motility.
source: A mutant deficient in the fcpA gene lost its ability to produce translational motility and to penetrate mucous membranes, resulting in loss of kidney colonization and lethality in the hamster model of leptospirosis.

claim: A mutant deficient in the fcpA gene lost its ability to penetrate mucous membranes.
source: A mutant deficient in the fcpA gene lost its ability to produce translational motility and to penetrate mucous membranes, resulting in loss of kidney colonization and lethality in the hamster model of leptospirosis.

claim: The fcpA mutant resulted in loss of kidney colonization in the hamster model of leptospirosis.
source: A mutant deficient in the fcpA gene lost its ability to produce translational motility and to penetrate mucous membranes, resulting in loss of kidney colonization and lethality in the hamster model of leptospirosis.

claim: The fcpA mutant resulted in loss of lethality in the hamster model of leptospirosis.
source: A mutant deficient in the fcpA gene lost its ability to produce translational motility and to penetrate mucous membranes, resulting in loss of kidney colonization and lethality in the hamster model of leptospirosis.

claim: A needle inoculation of the fcpA mutant produced a transient bacteremia prior to clearance by the host immune response.
source: Although highly attenuated in the hamster model, a needle inoculation of the mutant produced a transient bacteremia prior to clearance by the host immune response (Wunder et al., 2016a).

claim: DNA of the fcpA- mutant was detected in all tissues tested except the brain after subcutaneous inoculation of 10^7 leptospires in hamsters.
source: In this study, after inoculation of 107 leptospires using the subcutaneous route of infection in hamsters, we detected the presence of DNA of the mutant by qPCR in all the tissues tested, with the exception of the brain (Figure 1A).
evidence: Experimental data from qPCR analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The wild-type strain reached higher number of leptospires in all tissues analyzed compared to the fcpA- mutant.
source: These results were similar to those observed previously, with the wild-type reaching higher number of leptospires in all tissues analyzed, leading to the death or euthanasia of the animals due to clinical signs of disease 5–7 days after infection.
evidence: Experimental data comparing wild-type and mutant strains.

claim: Wild-type infection led to death or euthanasia of hamsters due to clinical signs of disease 5-7 days after infection.
source: These results were similar to those observed previously, with the wild-type reaching higher number of leptospires in all tissues analyzed, leading to the death or euthanasia of the animals due to clinical signs of disease 5–7 days after infection.

claim: The signal for the fcpA- mutant strain was undetectable after 7 days in hamsters.
source: In comparison, the signal for the fcpA- mutant strain was undetectable after 7 days with all inoculated animals surviving with no detectable leptospires in either kidney or blood, measured by qPCR and culture.
evidence: Experimental data from qPCR and culture.

claim: All hamsters inoculated with the fcpA- mutant survived with no detectable leptospires in kidney or blood after 7 days.
source: In comparison, the signal for the fcpA- mutant strain was undetectable after 7 days with all inoculated animals surviving with no detectable leptospires in either kidney or blood, measured by qPCR and culture.
evidence: Experimental data from qPCR and culture.

claim: No detectable signal was observed for animals immunized with the L1-130 heat-killed strain.
source: Similarly, no detectable signal was observed for the animals immunized with the L1-130 heat-killed strain (Figure 1A).

claim: The dose of wild-type strain was not enough to produce disease and lethality in infected mice.
source: Although the dose of the wild-type strain was not enough to produce disease and lethality on infected mice, all animals were colonized and the presence of the leptospiral DNA in blood was detectable until the fifteenth day after infection (Figure 1B).
evidence: Experimental observation from mouse model shown in Figure 1B.

claim: All mice infected with wild-type strain were colonized.
source: Although the dose of the wild-type strain was not enough to produce disease and lethality on infected mice, all animals were colonized and the presence of the leptospiral DNA in blood was detectable until the fifteenth day after infection (Figure 1B).
evidence: Experimental data from mouse model shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Leptospiral DNA in blood of wild-type infected mice was detectable until the fifteenth day after infection.
source: Although the dose of the wild-type strain was not enough to produce disease and lethality on infected mice, all animals were colonized and the presence of the leptospiral DNA in blood was detectable until the fifteenth day after infection (Figure 1B).
evidence: Experimental data from qPCR shown in Figure 1B.

claim: No dose of the fcpA- mutant caused colonization in mice.
source: Furthermore, no dose of the fcpA- mutant caused colonization (data not shown) and there was a significant difference in the magnitude of dissemination of the mutant in the blood compared to the wild type (Figure 1B).

claim: There was a significant difference in the magnitude of dissemination of the fcpA- mutant in the blood compared to the wild type in mice.
source: Furthermore, no dose of the fcpA- mutant caused colonization (data not shown) and there was a significant difference in the magnitude of dissemination of the mutant in the blood compared to the wild type (Figure 1B).

claim: DNA signal of the fcpA- mutant was only observed in the blood of mice infected with doses of 10^7 and 10^5 until the 13th and 8th day after infection, respectively.
source: DNA signal of the fcpA- mutant was only observed in the blood of animals infected with doses of 107 and 105 until the 13th and 8th day after infection, respectively.

claim: The fcpA- mutant is attenuated in both the hamster and mouse model.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that although the fcpA- mutant is attenuated in both the hamster and mouse model, there is a hematogenous dissemination of this mutant, identified by detection of its DNA.

claim: There is hematogenous dissemination of the fcpA- mutant.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that although the fcpA- mutant is attenuated in both the hamster and mouse model, there is a hematogenous dissemination of this mutant, identified by detection of its DNA.

claim: The fcpA- mutant appears to be cleared by the immune system before it results in observable disease or death of the animals.
source: The mutant appears to be cleared by the immune system before it results in observable disease or death of the animals.
evidence: Inference from survival and clearance data.

claim: The dissemination of the fcpA- mutant is dose dependent in the mouse model.
source: Furthermore, we observed in the mouse model that the dissemination of the mutant is dose dependent.

claim: The theoretic limit of detection of the qPCR assay used is 100 leptospires/mL of blood.
source: However, it is important to notice that although we do not see any signal of the mutant in doses equal or lower to 103 leptospires, the theoretic limit of detection of the qPCR assay used here (Wunder et al., 2016a; Stoddard et al., 2009) is 100 leptospires/mL of blood which can result in false negative results.

claim: Immunization with a single dose of the fcpA- mutant conferred complete protection against mortality in hamsters from infection with homologous and heterologous serovars.
source: Immunization with a single dose of the fcpA- mutant (Figure 2A) conferred complete protection against mortality in hamsters from infection with homologous and heterologous serovars (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Experimental data from vaccination and challenge studies shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Immunization with heat-killed leptospires conferred partial protection to the homologous but not against the heterologous serovar.
source: In contrast, immunization with heat-killed leptospires conferred partial protection to the homologous but not against the heterologous serovar (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Experimental data from vaccination and challenge studies shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Heat-killed bacterins can give a high protection level against an homologous challenge.
source: Heat-killed bacterins can give a high protection level against an homologous challenge (Adler, 2015), but usually the protocol for vaccination includes at least a second dose of the vaccine.

claim: The strain Hardjo 203 was described to cause only colonization in the hamster model infected by intraperitoneal route.
source: It is important to mention that the strain Hardjo 203 was described to cause only colonization in the hamster model infected by intraperitoneal route (Zuerner et al., 2012).

claim: In LD50 experiments using the conjunctival route, Hardjo 203 reproducibly caused 25% death rate.
source: However, in our LD50 experiments using the conjunctival route we reproducibly observed 25% death rate when using the conjunctival route (Supplementary file 1).

claim: In the non-vaccinated group, an overall death rate of 21.4% was observed after challenge with the strain Hardjo 203.
source: Furthermore, in the non-vaccinated group we observed an overall death rate of 21.4% after challenge with the strain Hardjo 203, but no deaths in the vaccinated group, which explains the wide 95% CI range (Figure 2B and Table S2).

claim: No deaths occurred in the vaccinated group after challenge with Hardjo 203.
source: Furthermore, in the non-vaccinated group we observed an overall death rate of 21.4% after challenge with the strain Hardjo 203, but no deaths in the vaccinated group, which explains the wide 95% CI range (Figure 2B and Table S2).

claim: Protection against renal colonization was observed in 80% of hamsters immunized with fcpA- mutant after homologous infection.
source: Protection against renal colonization was only observed in 80% of the animals immunized with fcpA- mutant after homologous infection.

claim: Heterologous infection gave varying levels of protection against colonization, from 0% to 35.7%.
source: Heterologous infection gave varying levels of protection, from 0% to 35.7% (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 2).

claim: Hamsters are highly susceptible to leptospirosis.
source: Hamsters are highly susceptible to leptospirosis (Haake, 2006), so the finding that the attenuated strain conferred partial protection against colonization was not unexpected.

claim: The protection conferred by the fcpA- mutant is dose dependent in mice.
source: Our results indicate that the protection conferred by the fcpA- mutant is dose dependent.

claim: The vaccine conferred 100% protection against death up to a dose of 10^3 leptospires of the fcpA- mutant in mice.
source: Against death, the vaccine conferred 100% protection up to a dose of 103 leptospires of the fcpA- mutant (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 3), but a dose as high as 107 leptospires was necessary to obtain 100% protection against colonization (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 3).

claim: A dose as high as 10^7 leptospires was necessary to obtain 100% protection against colonization in mice.
source: Against death, the vaccine conferred 100% protection up to a dose of 103 leptospires of the fcpA- mutant (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 3), but a dose as high as 107 leptospires was necessary to obtain 100% protection against colonization (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 3).

claim: There is a significant reduction of the burden of disease in hamsters after heterologous infection with the fcpA- mutant vaccine.
source: Furthermore, our quantitative analyzes of renal colonization showed that although the fcpA- mutant cannot promote complete protection, there is a significant reduction of the burden of the disease both in hamster after heterologous infection (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 2) and in lower doses of the vaccine in the mouse model, which also revealed a dose-dependent phenotype (Figure 2G and Supplementary file 3).

claim: There is a significant reduction of disease burden in lower doses of the vaccine in the mouse model with a dose-dependent phenotype.
source: Furthermore, our quantitative analyzes of renal colonization showed that although the fcpA- mutant cannot promote complete protection, there is a significant reduction of the burden of the disease both in hamster after heterologous infection (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 2) and in lower doses of the vaccine in the mouse model, which also revealed a dose-dependent phenotype (Figure 2G and Supplementary file 3).

claim: A single dose of a live attenuated-vaccine elicits cross-protective immunity against serovars belonging to L. interrogans, L. kirschneri, and L. borgpetersenii.
source: These findings indicate that a single dose of a live attenuated-vaccine elicits cross-protective immunity against serovars belonging to L. interrogans, L. kirschneri, and L. borgpetersenii, the species which encompasses the majority of serovars of human and animal health importance.
evidence: Inference from experimental protection data across species.

claim: L. interrogans, L. kirschneri, and L. borgpetersenii encompass the majority of serovars of human and animal health importance.
source: These findings indicate that a single dose of a live attenuated-vaccine elicits cross-protective immunity against serovars belonging to L. interrogans, L. kirschneri, and L. borgpetersenii, the species which encompasses the majority of serovars of human and animal health importance.

claim: The fcpA- attenuated-vaccine induced a weak agglutinating antibodies response to the homologous serovar, Copenhageni.
source: The fcpA- attenuated-vaccine induced a weak agglutinating antibodies response to the homologous serovar, Copenhageni, and undetectable microscopic agglutination test (MAT) titers against heterologous serovars, both in hamsters (Figure 3A) and mice (Figure 3C).
evidence: Experimental data from MAT shown in Figure 3A and 3C.

claim: The fcpA- attenuated-vaccine induced undetectable MAT titers against heterologous serovars in both hamsters and mice.
source: The fcpA- attenuated-vaccine induced a weak agglutinating antibodies response to the homologous serovar, Copenhageni, and undetectable microscopic agglutination test (MAT) titers against heterologous serovars, both in hamsters (Figure 3A) and mice (Figure 3C).
evidence: Experimental data from MAT shown in Figure 3A and 3C.

claim: In the mouse model, agglutinating antibodies were only measurable with a dose of at least 10^5 leptospires.
source: Furthermore, in the mouse model, agglutinating antibodies were only measurable with a dose of at least 105 leptospires (Figure 3C).
evidence: Experimental data from MAT shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A single dose of the fcpA- mutant was able to induce a robust immune response against leptospiral proteins.
source: In contrast, a single dose of the fcpA- mutant was able to induce a robust immune response against leptospiral proteins, recognizing proteins across the different species of Leptospira used in the hamster model (Figure 3B) and the heterologous strain used in the mouse model with a dose of at least 103 leptospires (Figure 3D).
evidence: Experimental data from western blot shown in Figure 3B and 3D.

claim: The fcpA- mutant induced recognition of proteins across different species of Leptospira.
source: In contrast, a single dose of the fcpA- mutant was able to induce a robust immune response against leptospiral proteins, recognizing proteins across the different species of Leptospira used in the hamster model (Figure 3B) and the heterologous strain used in the mouse model with a dose of at least 103 leptospires (Figure 3D).
evidence: Experimental data from western blot shown in Figure 3B and 3D.

claim: The presence of detectable antibodies measured by ELISA correlates with the highest dose that induced 100% protection against death in the mouse model (10^3 leptospires).
source: In addition, the presence of detectable antibodies measured by ELISA correlates with the highest dose that induced 100% protection against death in the mouse model (103 leptospires), and there is a decrease on the OD for all doses when the Manilae antigen was treated with proteinase K (Figure 3E).
evidence: Experimental data from ELISA shown in Figure 3E.

claim: There is a decrease in OD for all doses when the Manilae antigen was treated with proteinase K.
source: In addition, the presence of detectable antibodies measured by ELISA correlates with the highest dose that induced 100% protection against death in the mouse model (103 leptospires), and there is a decrease on the OD for all doses when the Manilae antigen was treated with proteinase K (Figure 3E).
evidence: Experimental data from ELISA shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Passive transfer experiments using hamster-immune sera against fcpA- attenuated-vaccine conferred 100% protection against heterologous lethal infection in hamsters.
source: Furthermore, our passive transfer experiments using hamster-immune sera against fcpA- attenuated-vaccine conferred 100% protection against heterologous lethal infection in hamsters (Figure 3F) and mice (Figure 3G).
evidence: Experimental data from passive transfer shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Passive transfer experiments using hamster-immune sera against fcpA- attenuated-vaccine conferred 100% protection against heterologous lethal infection in mice.
source: Furthermore, our passive transfer experiments using hamster-immune sera against fcpA- attenuated-vaccine conferred 100% protection against heterologous lethal infection in hamsters (Figure 3F) and mice (Figure 3G).
evidence: Experimental data from passive transfer shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Anti-Leptospira protein antibodies, and not agglutinating antibodies, are the correlate of vaccine-mediated cross-protective immunity.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that anti-Leptospira protein antibodies, and not agglutinating antibodies, are the correlate of vaccine-mediated cross-protective immunity.
evidence: Inference from combined experimental data on antibody responses and protection.

claim: A total of 133 protein targets were identified in hamsters immunized with a dose of 10^7 leptospires.
source: We identified a total of 133 (Figure 4A) and 56 (Figure 4B) protein targets on our analysis of hamsters (Hamster 107) and mice (Mouse 107) respectively, immunized with a dose of 107 leptospires and a total of 13 protein targets (Figure 4C) on our analysis of mouse immunized with different doses of the attenuated-vaccine (Mouse all).
evidence: Proteome array analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A total of 56 protein targets were identified in mice immunized with a dose of 10^7 leptospires.
source: We identified a total of 133 (Figure 4A) and 56 (Figure 4B) protein targets on our analysis of hamsters (Hamster 107) and mice (Mouse 107) respectively, immunized with a dose of 107 leptospires and a total of 13 protein targets (Figure 4C) on our analysis of mouse immunized with different doses of the attenuated-vaccine (Mouse all).
evidence: Proteome array analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: A total of 13 protein targets were identified in mice immunized with different doses of the attenuated-vaccine.
source: We identified a total of 133 (Figure 4A) and 56 (Figure 4B) protein targets on our analysis of hamsters (Hamster 107) and mice (Mouse 107) respectively, immunized with a dose of 107 leptospires and a total of 13 protein targets (Figure 4C) on our analysis of mouse immunized with different doses of the attenuated-vaccine (Mouse all).
evidence: Proteome array analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The three different analyses resulted in a total of 154 unique protein targets.
source: When combined, these three different analyses resulted in a total of 154 unique protein targets (Figure 4D and Supplementary file 4).

claim: Of the 154 protein targets, 55% have no prediction of localization.
source: Of those, 55% (85) have no prediction of localization and 23% (36), 14% (21), and 8% (12) have a prediction to be cytoplasmic membrane-associated, outer membrane proteins (OMP), and cytoplasmic, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Of the 154 protein targets, 23% are predicted to be cytoplasmic membrane-associated.
source: Of those, 55% (85) have no prediction of localization and 23% (36), 14% (21), and 8% (12) have a prediction to be cytoplasmic membrane-associated, outer membrane proteins (OMP), and cytoplasmic, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Of the 154 protein targets, 14% are predicted to be outer membrane proteins.
source: Of those, 55% (85) have no prediction of localization and 23% (36), 14% (21), and 8% (12) have a prediction to be cytoplasmic membrane-associated, outer membrane proteins (OMP), and cytoplasmic, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Of the 154 protein targets, 8% are predicted to be cytoplasmic.
source: Of those, 55% (85) have no prediction of localization and 23% (36), 14% (21), and 8% (12) have a prediction to be cytoplasmic membrane-associated, outer membrane proteins (OMP), and cytoplasmic, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Enrichment analysis showed a 5.0-fold enrichment for OMP (p=4.51E-10).
source: Enrichment analysis showed a 5.0-fold (p=4.51E-10) and 1.8-fold (p=2.92E-04) enrichment for OMP and cytoplasmic membrane-associated, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Enrichment analysis showed a 1.8-fold enrichment for cytoplasmic membrane-associated proteins (p=2.92E-04).
source: Enrichment analysis showed a 5.0-fold (p=4.51E-10) and 1.8-fold (p=2.92E-04) enrichment for OMP and cytoplasmic membrane-associated, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cytoplasmic proteins were 0.3-fold underrepresented in reactive antigens groups (p=2.91E-10).
source: In contrast, cytoplasmic proteins were 0.3-fold (p=2.91E-10) underrepresented in reactive antigens groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Proteins with predicted COG-U function were enriched by 4.9-fold (p=2.27E-07) among the reactive antigens.
source: Enrichment analysis identified proteins with predicted COG-U, COG-N, and COG-M function as highly enriched among the reactive antigens, by 4.9-fold (p=2.27E-07), 3.1-fold (p=8.35E-05), and 1.6-fold (p<0.05), respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Proteins with predicted COG-N function were enriched by 3.1-fold (p=8.35E-05) among the reactive antigens.
source: Enrichment analysis identified proteins with predicted COG-U, COG-N, and COG-M function as highly enriched among the reactive antigens, by 4.9-fold (p=2.27E-07), 3.1-fold (p=8.35E-05), and 1.6-fold (p<0.05), respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Proteins with predicted COG-M function were enriched by 1.6-fold (p<0.05) among the reactive antigens.
source: Enrichment analysis identified proteins with predicted COG-U, COG-N, and COG-M function as highly enriched among the reactive antigens, by 4.9-fold (p=2.27E-07), 3.1-fold (p=8.35E-05), and 1.6-fold (p<0.05), respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Proteins predicted to be involved in signal transduction mechanisms (COG-T) were significantly underrepresented in reactive antigens by 0.4-fold (p=0.016).
source: Furthermore, proteins predicted to be involved in signal transduction mechanisms (COG-T) and in amino acid transport and metabolism (COG-E) were significantly underrepresented in reactive antigens, by 0.4-fold (p=0.016) and 0.3-fold (0.02), respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Proteins predicted to be involved in amino acid transport and metabolism (COG-E) were significantly underrepresented in reactive antigens by 0.3-fold (p=0.02).
source: Furthermore, proteins predicted to be involved in signal transduction mechanisms (COG-T) and in amino acid transport and metabolism (COG-E) were significantly underrepresented in reactive antigens, by 0.4-fold (p=0.016) and 0.3-fold (0.02), respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Statistical enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The enrichment analysis validates the approach to identify biologically relevant protein candidates for a cross-protective vaccine.
source: Taken together, the enrichment analysis validates our approach to identify biologically relevant protein candidates for a cross-protective vaccine.

claim: 41 protein targets were identified based on their relationship among the three different groups of the proteome array's analysis.
source: We were able to narrow down the identified 154 proteins to 41 protein targets based on their relationship among the three different groups of the proteome array's analysis (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Seven proteins were identified in all three analysis groups.
source: Seven proteins were identified in all groups (Figures 4D and 5 and Supplementary file 4, red) and 31 proteins were identified in both hamster and mouse vaccinated with a dose of 107 leptospires of the attenuated-vaccine (Figures 4D and 5 and Supplementary file 4, yellow).

claim: 31 proteins were identified in both hamster and mouse vaccinated with a dose of 10^7 leptospires of the attenuated-vaccine.
source: Seven proteins were identified in all groups (Figures 4D and 5 and Supplementary file 4, red) and 31 proteins were identified in both hamster and mouse vaccinated with a dose of 107 leptospires of the attenuated-vaccine (Figures 4D and 5 and Supplementary file 4, yellow).

claim: Hamster and mice immune sera were highly reactive to the majority of the 41 proteins.
source: Hamster and mice immune sera were highly reactive to the majority of the 41 proteins (Figure 5), in contrast to the low reactivity for the control sera and animals vaccinated with the heat-killed vaccine (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating the ability of the attenuated-vaccine to induce immunity against leptospiral proteins.
evidence: Proteome array data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Control sera and animals vaccinated with the heat-killed vaccine showed low reactivity to the 41 proteins.
source: Hamster and mice immune sera were highly reactive to the majority of the 41 proteins (Figure 5), in contrast to the low reactivity for the control sera and animals vaccinated with the heat-killed vaccine (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating the ability of the attenuated-vaccine to induce immunity against leptospiral proteins.
evidence: Proteome array data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The attenuated-vaccine has the ability to induce immunity against leptospiral proteins.
source: Hamster and mice immune sera were highly reactive to the majority of the 41 proteins (Figure 5), in contrast to the low reactivity for the control sera and animals vaccinated with the heat-killed vaccine (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating the ability of the attenuated-vaccine to induce immunity against leptospiral proteins.
evidence: Inference from proteome array reactivity data.

claim: Six OMPs were identified among the 41 seroreactive proteins.
source: We identified plausible vaccine candidates among these 41 seroreactive proteins (Figure 5), which included six OMPs and known putative virulence factors such as LipL32, LipL41, and Lig proteins (Ko et al., 2009; Picardeau, 2017), providing supportive evidence for using proteome arrays to identify such proteins.
evidence: Analysis of the 41 proteins shown in Figure 5.

claim: Known putative virulence factors such as LipL32, LipL41, and Lig proteins were identified among the 41 seroreactive proteins.
source: We identified plausible vaccine candidates among these 41 seroreactive proteins (Figure 5), which included six OMPs and known putative virulence factors such as LipL32, LipL41, and Lig proteins (Ko et al., 2009; Picardeau, 2017), providing supportive evidence for using proteome arrays to identify such proteins.
evidence: Analysis of the 41 proteins shown in Figure 5, with citation to published literature.

claim: 40% of the 41 seroreactive proteins are identified as hypothetical proteins with no described function.
source: Not surprisingly, 40% of those targets are identified as hypothetical proteins with no described function.

claim: 70% of the 41 proteins have high amino acid sequence identity (>80%) among their respective orthologs in all 13 pathogenic Leptospira species analyzed.
source: However, the majority (70%) have high amino acid sequence identity (>80%) among their respective orthologs in all the 13 pathogenic Leptospira species analyzed (Figure 5), and therefore may be targeted for eliciting cross-protective responses.

claim: Sera from confirmed patients with acute leptospirosis reacted with 17 of the 41 Leptospira proteins recognized by sera from animals immunized with the attenuated-vaccine.
source: Moreover, sera from confirmed patients with acute leptospirosis reacted with 17 of the 41 Leptospira proteins recognized by sera from animals immunized with the attenuated-vaccine (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Proteome array data with human sera shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: This is the first study showing evidence of cross-protection across species with a vaccine in leptospirosis.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first study showing evidence of cross-protection across species with a vaccine in leptospirosis.
evidence: Authors' assessment of the novelty of their findings.

claim: A single high-dose of the fcpA- mutant induced sterilizing immunity in the mice model of leptospirosis.
source: A single high-dose of the fcpA- mutant induced sterilizing immunity in the mice model of leptospirosis.
evidence: Experimental data from mouse vaccination and challenge studies.

claim: Whole-cell vaccines have shown divergent levels of protection against colonization in different species.
source: Whole-cell vaccines have shown divergent levels of protection against colonization in different species (Sonada et al., 2018; Murray et al., 2013; Clough et al., 2018; Bolin and Alt, 2001).

claim: A significant reduction of the bacterial burden in the kidney of vaccinated hamsters was observed.
source: In our hamster model we observed a significant reduction of the bacterial burden in the kidney of vaccinated animals, without significant levels of protection.
evidence: Experimental data from hamster colonization studies.

claim: Mice models are good alternatives for sublethal leptospirosis infection and particularly to study renal colonization, compared to the highly susceptible hamster model.
source: Mice models are good alternatives for sublethal leptospirosis infection and particularly to study renal colonization, compared to the highly susceptible hamster model (Gomes-Solecki et al., 2017).

claim: The mice model lacks information about susceptibility to a wide range of strains compared to hamsters.
source: However, the mice model lacks information about susceptibility to a wide range of strains compared to hamsters (Gomes-Solecki et al., 2017), and for that reason we were only able to test serovar Manilae as an heterologous model to the serovar Copenhageni attenuated-vaccine.

claim: If the challenge dose is not able to cause death of mice, a portion of the sublethal dose of leptospires is able to escape the blood defenses and colonize the kidneys.
source: Previous experiments in mice showed that if the challenge dose is not able to cause death of the animals, a portion of the sublethal dose of leptospires is able to escape the blood defenses and colonize the kidneys (Ratet et al., 2014).

claim: The dose of infection necessary to cause disease in natural infection remains unclear.
source: Furthermore, the dose of infection necessary to cause disease in natural infection remains unclear, although recent research showed that the numbers of leptospires available in the environment are low on average (Casanovas-Massana et al., 2018b; Ganoza et al., 2006).

claim: The numbers of leptospires available in the environment are low on average.
source: Furthermore, the dose of infection necessary to cause disease in natural infection remains unclear, although recent research showed that the numbers of leptospires available in the environment are low on average (Casanovas-Massana et al., 2018b; Ganoza et al., 2006).

claim: Current animal model experiments focus on unrealistic high challenge doses, which can devaluate vaccine efficacy estimation.
source: Current animal model experiments focus on unrealistic high challenge doses, which can devaluate vaccine efficacy estimation.

claim: The fcpA- attenuated-vaccine is able to induce a robust sterilizing immunity capable of preventing death and colonization after a high lethal dose of infection.
source: Despite that, our results indicate that the fcpA- attenuated-vaccine is able to induce a robust sterilizing immunity capable of preventing death and colonization after a high lethal dose of infection.

claim: The essential role of antibodies for protection against leptospirosis has been long described.
source: The essential role of antibodies for protection against leptospirosis has been long described (Adler et al., 1980; Inada et al., 1916).

claim: There have been no attempts to address whether naturally acquired infection elicits immunity to reinfection in either humans or animals.
source: However, the key knowledge gap for vaccine development is whether naturally acquired infection elicits immunity to reinfection. There have been no attempts to address this question in either humans or animals and our understanding has thus relied solely on experimental models of acquired immunity.
evidence: Authors' assessment of the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Passive transfer experiments have shown that whole-cell vaccine immunity is antibody-mediated.
source: Passive transfer experiments have shown that whole-cell vaccine immunity is antibody-mediated (Inada et al., 1916; Adler, 2015).

claim: Serovar-specific protection correlates with agglutinating antibody titers.
source: Serovar-specific protection correlates with agglutinating antibody titers (Adler et al., 1980; Chapman et al., 1991), which are directed against lipopolysaccharides (LPS) (Challa et al., 2011).

claim: Agglutinating antibody titers are directed against lipopolysaccharides (LPS).
source: Serovar-specific protection correlates with agglutinating antibody titers (Adler et al., 1980; Chapman et al., 1991), which are directed against lipopolysaccharides (LPS) (Challa et al., 2011).

claim: Anti-leptospiral LPS antibodies are generated by whole-cell based vaccines.
source: Anti-leptospiral LPS antibodies are generated by whole-cell based vaccines, and the restricted protection these vaccines confer is one of their major limitations (Adler, 2015).

claim: The restricted protection conferred by whole-cell vaccines is one of their major limitations.
source: Anti-leptospiral LPS antibodies are generated by whole-cell based vaccines, and the restricted protection these vaccines confer is one of their major limitations (Adler, 2015).

claim: Immunization with an attenuated, LPS-deficient strain of serovar Manilae conferred protection against infection with serovar Pomona and other L. interrogans species.
source: Recently, immunization with an attenuated, LPS-deficient strain of serovar Manilae conferred protection against infection with serovar Pomona and other L. interrogans species, suggesting that anti-Leptospira protein responses are indeed cross-protective (Srikram et al., 2011; Murray et al., 2018).

claim: Anti-Leptospira protein responses are cross-protective.
source: Recently, immunization with an attenuated, LPS-deficient strain of serovar Manilae conferred protection against infection with serovar Pomona and other L. interrogans species, suggesting that anti-Leptospira protein responses are indeed cross-protective (Srikram et al., 2011; Murray et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from published literature and supported by current study results.

claim: The cross-protection mediated by anti-protein antibodies is transferable.
source: Our results not only corroborate those previous studies, but also shows strong evidence, through passive transfer experiments, that the cross-protection mediated by anti-protein antibodies is transferable.
evidence: Experimental data from passive transfer experiments.

claim: The attenuated-vaccine induced a robust anti-Leptospira protein antibody response.
source: The attenuated-vaccine induced a robust anti-Leptospira protein antibody response, but these antibodies recognized a limited repertoire of 154 antigens.

claim: The antibodies induced by the attenuated-vaccine recognized a limited repertoire of 154 antigens.
source: The attenuated-vaccine induced a robust anti-Leptospira protein antibody response, but these antibodies recognized a limited repertoire of 154 antigens.

claim: A previous similar study reported 11 proteins.
source: Although the numbers in our study are higher compared to the 11 proteins reported by a similar study (Srikram et al., 2011), this difference likely relates to the significantly higher sensitivity of the proteome array compared to the 2-DIGE method used previously.

claim: The difference in number of proteins identified relates to the significantly higher sensitivity of the proteome array compared to the 2-DIGE method.
source: Although the numbers in our study are higher compared to the 11 proteins reported by a similar study (Srikram et al., 2011), this difference likely relates to the significantly higher sensitivity of the proteome array compared to the 2-DIGE method used previously.

claim: The approach was validated by the enrichment analysis of the reactive proteins.
source: Nevertheless, our approach was validated by the enrichment analysis of the reactive proteins, which showed that proteins classified as OMP and cytoplasmic membrane-associated, and proteins predicted to be involved in cell wall/membrane and intracellular trafficking/secretion were highly enriched among the selected proteins.

claim: Using two animal models and different doses of the vaccine allowed reduction of the number of proteins to 41 selected proteins.
source: Moreover, using two animal models and different doses of the vaccine allowed us to reduce this number to 41 selected proteins, characterizing correlates of immunity.

claim: Immunization with Lig proteins or LipL32 has been shown to confer protection against experimental infection.
source: Immunization with Lig proteins or LipL32 (Conrad et al., 2017; Ko et al., 2009; Humphryes et al., 2014) has been shown to confer protection, albeit not cross-protective immunity, against experimental infection.

claim: Immunization with Lig proteins or LipL32 does not confer cross-protective immunity.
source: Immunization with Lig proteins or LipL32 (Conrad et al., 2017; Ko et al., 2009; Humphryes et al., 2014) has been shown to confer protection, albeit not cross-protective immunity, against experimental infection.

claim: Efficacy results with Lig proteins or LipL32 have been proven difficult to replicate.
source: However, efficacy results have been proven difficult to replicate (Deveson Lucas et al., 2011; Ko et al., 2009).

claim: Studies have shown that a chimeric approach has the potential for an effective universal vaccine against leptospirosis.
source: Lately, studies have shown that a chimeric approach has the potential for an effective universal vaccine against leptospirosis (Lin et al., 2016; Santos and Nascimento, 2018).

claim: LipL41 has been tested as a vaccine candidate without success.
source: Other than Ligs and LipL32, LipL41 has been tested as a vaccine candidate without success (Ko et al., 2009) and LIC20172 and LIC11966 have been identified and tested, respectively, as promising candidates for subunit vaccine (Lata et al., 2018; Oliveira et al., 2018).

claim: LIC20172 and LIC11966 have been identified and tested as promising candidates for subunit vaccine.
source: Other than Ligs and LipL32, LipL41 has been tested as a vaccine candidate without success (Ko et al., 2009) and LIC20172 and LIC11966 have been identified and tested, respectively, as promising candidates for subunit vaccine (Lata et al., 2018; Oliveira et al., 2018).

claim: A DNA vaccine delivering two leptospiral proteins (RecA and FliD) has shown promising results including high survival rates, sterilizing immunity and heterologous protection.
source: More recently, a DNA vaccine delivering two leptospiral proteins (RecA and FliD) has shown promising results including high survival rates, sterilizing immunity and heterologous protection, although tested only among two different L. interrogans strains (Raja et al., 2018).

claim: A major limitation for vaccine development for leptospirosis is the lack of evidence whether immunological correlates from experimental animals are relevant to human disease.
source: A major limitation for vaccine development for leptospirosis is the lack of evidence whether immunological correlates from experimental animals are relevant to human disease.
evidence: Assessment of the state of the field.

claim: The same antigens that confer cross-protective immunity in the attenuated-vaccine model may play a role in naturally acquired immunity in humans.
source: However, our results suggest that the same antigens that confer cross-protective immunity in the attenuated-vaccine model may play a role in naturally acquired immunity in humans.
evidence: Inference from human sera reactivity data.

claim: This study is the first description of vaccine that elicits cross-protection against disease caused by different species of the genus Leptospira.
source: This study is the first description of vaccine that elicits cross-protection against disease caused by different species of the genus Leptospira, and that the protection is transferable through anti-protein antibodies.
evidence: Authors' assessment of the novelty of their findings.

claim: The protection is transferable through anti-protein antibodies.
source: This study is the first description of vaccine that elicits cross-protection against disease caused by different species of the genus Leptospira, and that the protection is transferable through anti-protein antibodies.
evidence: Experimental data from passive transfer experiments.

claim: The fcpA- mutant induced robust and cross-protective immune responses against protein moieties conserved across pathogenic Leptospira.
source: The fcpA- mutant induced robust and cross-protective immune responses against protein moieties conserved across pathogenic Leptospira.

claim: A small repertoire of biologically relevant proteins can be used in the field of vaccine and diagnostic development for leptospirosis.
source: We identified a small repertoire of biologically relevant proteins that can be used in the field of vaccine and diagnostic development for leptospirosis.

claim: Characterization of these proteins as novel putative virulence factors can provide new insights on the pathogenesis of the disease.
source: Characterization of these proteins as novel putative virulence factors can also provide new insights on the pathogenesis of the disease.

claim: Live attenuated-vaccines are one of the most universal vaccination technologies used for the prevention of important bacterial diseases like tuberculosis, cholera, and salmonellosis and viruses like yellow fever, influenza, and zoster.
source: Live attenuated-vaccines are one of the most universal vaccination technologies used for the prevention of important bacterial diseases like tuberculosis, cholera, and salmonellosis and viruses like yellow fever, influenza, and zoster (Minor, 2015; Detmer and Glenting, 2006).

claim: An effective vaccine against leptospirosis would provide interdependent health and societal benefits by preventing transmission and disease in livestock and domestic animals and reducing the risk of spill-over infections in humans.
source: An effective vaccine against leptospirosis would provide interdependent health and societal benefits by preventing transmission and disease in livestock and domestic animals and reducing the risk of spill-over infections in humans.
evidence: Inference about potential public health impact.

claim: The first live attenuated-vaccine for leptospirosis with a defined mutation has been recently described.
source: The first live attenuated-vaccine for leptospirosis with a defined mutation has been recently described (Srikram et al., 2011; Murray et al., 2018) showing cross-protective immunity in hamsters and the potential for this approach.

claim: Immunization with an attenuated, LPS-deficient strain of serovar Manilae conferred varied levels of cross-protection against different species after one or two doses of the attenuated-vaccine.
source: These authors made the important finding that immunization with an attenuated, LPS-deficient strain of serovar Manilae conferred varied levels of cross-protection against different species after one or two doses of the attenuated-vaccine.

claim: A single dose of a flagella-less mutant in Borrelia burgdorferi induced homologous protection in mouse.
source: In another spirochete, a similar approach has been successfully explored when a single dose of a flagella-less mutant in Borrelia burgdorferi induced homologous protection in mouse (Sadziene et al., 1996).

claim: A target mutant in B. burgdorferi induced cross immunity, but four immunizations were necessary for full protection.
source: More recently, a target mutant in B. burgdorferi induced cross immunity, but four immunizations were necessary for full protection (Hahn et al., 2016).

claim: Previous work with attenuated-vaccine in Leptospira showed evidence of protection against homologous challenge in guinea-pigs, cattle, hamsters, and swine.
source: Previous work with attenuated-vaccine in Leptospira showed evidence of protection against homologous challenge in guinea-pigs, cattle, hamsters, and swine, but only partial cross-protection in hamsters and gerbils (Adler, 2015; Srikram et al., 2011).

claim: Previous work with attenuated-vaccine in Leptospira showed only partial cross-protection in hamsters and gerbils.
source: Previous work with attenuated-vaccine in Leptospira showed evidence of protection against homologous challenge in guinea-pigs, cattle, hamsters, and swine, but only partial cross-protection in hamsters and gerbils (Adler, 2015; Srikram et al., 2011).
